stage1.impression: A clean, symmetrical home-cinema or showroom render: two dark speakers stand as silhouettes against a bright, evenly lit fir-lined niche, with a dark, featureless carpet in front and smooth, untextured tub chairs. The Orb lamp is blown to a white disc, the left screen is brighter than the hero, there is no visible haze, concrete, beam or steel, and the signs of life don't read. A design magazine would not publish this as a specific place. It reads as a generic hi-fi demo room, not Planet EARF.

blocking_9: The speakers must be the brightest-read objects, not silhouettes: speaker region lum_median >= 45, with light visibly passing through the smoked acrylic and the white batts legible
The niche wall and soffit must not clip (clip_pct < 1 in the soffit band) and must fall off from the spots rather than glow evenly
The shell must be in frame: fir beams overhead, board-formed concrete and blackened steel, each reading at 1:1 as the real material
The carpet, velvet chairs and fir boards need real surface variation (pile, sheen, board-to-board tone, grain) with no tiled or smooth CG look
The Orb lamps must read as frosted acrylic with a glowing liner, not a clipped white disc
Visible, readable signs of life (the glass and record on the table, the coat over a chair, a sleeve that reads as printed card)
A little visible atmosphere in the spot cones; the frame should read as a specific room, not a generic demo room

defects.what: Niche soffit and top of the fir wall blown: 18.7 % clipped, two hot spots above the speakers
Niche side return evenly bright (median 168), with no falloff; reads like a lightbox
Right speaker a dark silhouette (median 20.6); the acrylic body reads as black glass, with no light through it
Orb lamp a clipped white disc (18.4 % clipped); no frosted-liner gradient, reads as a puck light
Wall screen brighter than the speakers (median 115) and slightly magenta; pulls the eye off the hero
Carpet a flat, uniform brown plane with no pile, wear or light pools; reads as a CG floor
Foreground tub chairs crushed (55.6 % crush), smooth CG velvet with no sheen or nap
Left tub chairs crushed and untextured
Fir boards uniform in tone and grain from board to board; reads as repeated veneer texture
Record sleeve against the plinth reads as a flat grey card
Top of frame: beam and ceiling almost black (crush 46 % at top left); shell materials not legible
No visible haze despite the spots; no concrete or blackened steel anywhere in frame
Hex table and props in the foreground read as a smooth slab; the glass is barely readable and no record is visible

changes.problem: The niche is the brightest thing in the frame and clips, so the speakers read as silhouettes against it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 174.6, clip_pct 18.7; niche wall 390-1020 x 150-500 median 93 vs speaker median 20

changes.expected: Soffit no longer clips; the fir wall drops to a warm mid-tone around 45-60, with the spots' pools doing the work

changes.problem: The speakers are front-dark: the altar spots light the wall behind them, not their faces and acrylic.

change.setting: the altar 2 x spot, and the lamps on each speaker
change.from: 70 W, 30 deg, aimed at the niche; speaker area lamps 0.1 W/m2
change.to: aim the altar spots at each speaker's front at 1.0 m height from the seat side, 110 W, cone 24 deg; the speaker area lamps 0.5 W/m2 so the smoked acrylic glows from inside

changes.expected: Speaker bodies read as smoked translucent acrylic with batts and the woofer cone legible; speaker median above 45

changes.problem: The Orb lamp is a clipped white disc that reads as a puck light, not frosted acrylic.
changes.expected: The Orb shows a soft gradient across the frosted liner, edge to centre, with the smoked shell visible around it

changes.problem: The frame shows none of the shell (beams, concrete, steel) and is a symmetrical showroom elevation, so it reads as generic.

evidence.measured: top band median 3.4, crush 46 %; no concrete or steel anywhere in frame

change.to: seated height z 1.15, 28 mm, keep level with a vertical lens shift up about 0.12 so the fir beams cross the top of the frame; move to y about 2.4 so the frame runs off-axis and catches the concrete side wall and a blackened-steel edge, with one tub chair and a hex table with its Orb close in the foreground

changes.expected: The beams, concrete and steel are legible; the pair sits off-centre in depth; the room reads as a specific place

changes.problem: The wall screen outshines the hero and adds the frame's only cool or magenta cast.
changes.expected: The screen sits as a dim, neutral image below the speakers' brightness

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere: the spots have no visible cones and the depth is flat.

evidence.measured: y-profile drops from 178 to 60 in one bin with no cone gradient; no veil visible over the dark carpet

changes.expected: Faint cones under the altar spots and Dome downlights; the blacks lift slightly in depth; the frame median stays at 28-45

changes.problem: The carpet, velvet tub chairs and fir boards are smooth, uniform CG surfaces.

evidence.measured: floor lum_range 89 with no local texture visible at 1:1; foreground chairs crush 55.6 %

change.from: uniform carpet and velvet; identical fir boards
change.to: carpet with a pile normal map at real scale and a 10 % low-frequency tone variation; velvet with sheen 0.6 and sheen tint so the edges catch the Orbs; per-board random tone of +/-12 % and varied grain offset on the fir, with a few checks and darker nail holes

changes.expected: The chairs read as espresso velvet with lit rims, the carpet shows pile and soft pools, and the fir reads as real boards

changes.problem: The signs of life don't read: the sleeve is a grey card, and the glass, record and coat are lost in the dark.

evidence.measured: sleeve flat grey; foreground table props barely visible beside the clipped Orb

change.from: sleeve against the plinth as a plain card; glass and record lost in the dark
change.to: give the sleeve a worn printed cover (muted, low saturation); put the record and a half-full rocks glass within the Orb's pool on the foreground table; drape the coat over the nearest tub chair arm so it catches the light

changes.expected: At least two signs of life read at a glance, with no saturated colour competing with the speakers

out_of_scope.request: Make the speakers' smoked tint lighter or warmer so they separate from the room
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour is fixed (Smoke configuration); separation has to come from light, as in c2

out_of_scope.request: Remove or soften the glowing white edge under each plinth
out_of_scope.why: The light plinth glowing under each speaker is part of the room's design as fixed

out_of_scope.request: Show one speaker rather than the pair
out_of_scope.why: The altar pair is fixed; the brief's 'one colour' is satisfied because both are the same product
